# Spark plug and intake gasket replacement

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove the engine cover, intake plenum, and ignition coils to replace spark plugs and gaskets. [t67]

[Partial] Remove electric throttle control actuator to detach intake manifold collector for spark plug and intake plenum gasket replacement. [t67]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the electric throttle control actuator to detach the intake manifold collector.
2. Spray brake cleaner on the plenum and let it soak for a while.
3. [Partial] Scrub the soaked area with a flexible bristle bottle washer.
4. Rinse the plenum with citric-based cleaner, then rinse thoroughly with water.
5. [Partial] Allow the plenum to dry completely before reassembly.

_Procedure reported by [t67]._

## Specifications

- **Ignition coil bolt torque**: 4-5 ft-lb (62 in-lb) [t67] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Spark plug torque**: 18 ft-lb [t67] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Start on the passenger side first as it requires more disassembly than the driver side. [t67]
- [Partial] Use a box wrench and pry bar trick to loosen tight bracket bolts if a socket is unavailable. [t67]
- [Partial] Mark coil wires with tape before removal to ensure correct reinstallation order. [t67]
- Consider removing the electric throttle control actuator to avoid dealing with attached anti-freeze coolant hoses. [t67]
- Use a propane torch or soapy water spray bottle to check for air and vacuum leaks after reassembly. [t67]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Yanking connections too hard when swinging the intake over the radiator, potentially severing hoses. [t67]
- [Partial] Forgetting that some lower throttle body hoses might need draining if following strict factory manual steps. [t67]
- Stripping bolts due to using a cheap torque wrench while rushed. [t67]
- Overtorquing the #3 ignition coil bolt, requiring Loctite afterward. [t67]
- [Partial] Snapping off the #3 intake manifold collector bolt and other duct/resonator bolts. [t67]
